nodes.title: The octonion model of G₂
nodes.statement: For a characteristic-zero field F, define Aut(O) on the existing split Octonion F by F-linear equivalences fixing 1 and preserving the ordered product. Represent this functor by an affine smooth connected group and identify it, with a chosen pinning, with the split Chevalley group of type G₂. It is simultaneously simply connected and adjoint; its 7-dimensional module is ker(trace).
hypotheses: The algebraic construction is over a characteristic-zero field unless a complex dual group is specified; orbit statements use the split octonion algebra. Local absolute values and smooth modules refer to the fixed p-adic convention.
proofSteps: Use polynomial multiplication-preservation equations in GL₈; derive preservation of trace and norm from the quadratic identity x²=tr(x)x−N(x)1.
Compare the torus and six positive root subgroups in the Zorn model with the Chevalley pinning; prove the map on groups, rather than infer a group isomorphism only from Der(O).
acceptance: Check that conjugation is not an automorphism although it preserves the norm.

sources.match: GS introduces the split octonion algebra with its conjugation, norm and trace, defines G₂ as its automorphism group, records that this group is split of rank two and both simply connected and adjoint, and fixes simple roots and a torus coordinate. The representability, the pinned comparison with the Chevalley group and the identification of the 7-dimensional module with the trace-zero part are the construction this node adds on the Tau Ceti carrier.

nodes.title: Null subspaces of the imaginary octonions
nodes.statement: A null subspace W of O means W≤ker(trace) and xy=0 for every ordered pair x,y∈W. Every such W has dimension at most two. G₂(F) is transitive on null lines, null planes and incident line-plane flags in the split algebra.

proofSteps: Use the Zorn multiplication and the polar form of N to classify mutually annihilating trace-zero vectors.
Reduce a nonzero null vector to a standard Zorn vector using elementary long and short root operations, then compute its annihilator to classify planes.
acceptance: A norm-isotropic subspace containing an idempotent is rejected.

nodes.title: The two G₂ parabolics and their radicals
nodes.statement: Choose simple roots α short and β long. Put P=MN for the stabilizer of a null plane and Q=LU for a null line in an incident flag, so P∩Q=B. Both Levis are GL₂; δP=|det|³ and δQ=|det|⁵. N is Heisenberg of dimension 5 with center U₍₃α₊₂β₎ and N/Z=Sym³(F²)⊗det⁻¹. U has graded pieces F², det, F²⊗det and nilpotency class 3. Its center is U₍₃α₊β₎U₍₃α₊₂β₎; U/Z(U), rather than U/[U,U], is Heisenberg.
hypotheses: The algebraic construction is over a characteristic-zero field unless a complex dual group is specified; orbit statements use the split octonion algebra. Local absolute values and smooth modules refer to the fixed p-adic convention.
proofSteps: Compute radicals as products of positive root groups and their commutators.
Sum radical weights: 2ρP=3(3α+2β), 2ρQ=5(2α+β); identify Levi modules by highest weights.
acceptance: Verify the central layer has dimension 2 for U and dimension 1 for N.

The node adds the centre of U and the correction that U/Z(U) is the Heisenberg quotient (packet E12).

nodes.title: Cubic étale Fourier data
nodes.statement: Identify generic characters of N(F) trivial on its center with nonzero-discriminant binary cubics using ψ and the dual of Sym³(F²)⊗det⁻¹. Their M(F)-orbits correspond to cubic étale F-algebras E. Choose ψE in each orbit; π_(N,ψE) is the existing twisted coinvariant quotient and W_E(π)=Hom_N(π,ψE). The choice is transported by conjugation, not made into a canonical basis.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Use the binary-cubic orbit correspondence and equivariance of twisted coinvariants. Pin the trace pairing and ψ so that ψ and its conjugate cannot be exchanged silently.
acceptance: Check the three cubic splitting types and the contragredient character.

nodes.title: Long-root SL₃ and unitary stabilizers
nodes.statement: The long-root subgroup in G₂ is SL₃, the pointwise stabilizer of the split quadratic subalgebra F×F⊂O. Its setwise stabilizer is SL₃⋊C₂ with pinned outer action. A quadratic field K⊂O has pointwise stabilizer the quasi-split SU₃(K/F) and setwise stabilizer SU₃(K/F)⋊C₂.
hypotheses: The algebraic construction is over a characteristic-zero field unless a complex dual group is specified; orbit statements use the split octonion algebra. Local absolute values and smooth modules refer to the fixed p-adic convention.
proofSteps: Use the decomposition O=K⊕K⊥ and the induced 3-dimensional K-hermitian space; compute the determinant condition and the normalizing conjugation.
acceptance: Separate pointwise from setwise stabilizers and the split from nonsplit quadratic algebra.

nodes.title: Exceptional inclusions of complex dual groups
nodes.statement: Using the existing dual root datum construction, identify G₂∨=G₂(C), PGL₃∨=SL₃(C), and PGSp₆∨=Spin₇(C). Construct SL₃→G₂→Spin₇ compatibly with the octonion 7-module and spin 8-module. In G₂, the centralizers Z_G₂(SL₃)=μ₃ and Z_G₂(SO₃)=μ₃⋊C₂=S₃; the commuting long- and short-root SL₂ factors give (SL₂,l×SL₂,s)/μ₂=SO₄.
hypotheses: The algebraic construction is over a characteristic-zero field unless a complex dual group is specified; orbit statements use the split octonion algebra. Local absolute values and smooth modules refer to the fixed p-adic convention.
proofSteps: Compare weight lattices and root subgroups, compute centralizers on the octonion decomposition, and identify G₂ as a nonisotropic spinor stabilizer.
acceptance: The dual of PGSp₆ is Spin₇, so its center μ₂ must remain visible.

nodes.title: Complex local parameters
nodes.statement: For a split connected reductive group with pinned dual Ĝ, a complex L-parameter is a Ĝ-conjugacy class of homomorphisms W_F×SL₂(C)→Ĝ(C), continuous on W_F with finite inertia image, semisimple on Frobenius and algebraic on SL₂; the two restrictions commute. Tempered means bounded Weil image; discrete means not contained in any proper Levi. Use the existing topological Weil group; |w|=q^(−deg w) for arithmetic Frobenius degree 1. This is not an integral parameter stack and is not a proof of LLC.
hypotheses: F is a nonarchimedean characteristic-zero local field and the dual algebraic group is over C; the topological local Weil group is the imported one.
proofSteps: Form the representation type on the imported Weil carrier and complex dual group.
Prove the dictionary with Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne pairs, including r(w)Nr(w)⁻¹=|w|N after fixing the SL₂-to-WD twist.
acceptance: Steinberg parameters have nontrivial Deligne SL₂ even when their Weil part is unramified.

sources.match: Gan–Savin define, for a split group, L-parameters as G∨-conjugacy classes of homomorphisms from W_F × SL₂(ℂ) to the dual group and state the shape of the local Langlands conjecture.

nodes.statement: For a complex parameter φ put Sraw(φ)=π₀Z_Ĝ(im φ) and Ssplit(φ)=π₀(Z_Ĝ(im φ)/Z(Ĝ)). Retain the raw group and the map to the quotient. Enhancements for the split form have trivial action on the image of the dual center; a specified inner form instead imposes its Kottwitz central character on the appropriate refined centralizer. For G₂ the center is trivial; for PGSp₆ explicitly divide by Z(Spin₇)=μ₂. This definition fixes bookkeeping, not an unproved parametrization of packets for all groups.

nodes.title: The 15-dimensional PGSp₆ Jordan model
nodes.statement: Let V=F⁶ with symplectic pairs (1,6),(2,5),(3,4). Put J=∧²V⊗ν⁻¹ with its Pfaffian cubic, unit e=x16+x25+x34, and structure group SL₆/μ₂. The unit stabilizer is PGSp₆. The stabilizers P_i of standard isotropic i-planes have M₃≅GL₃ via its action on ⟨x12,x13,x23⟩, M₂≅(GL₂×GL₂)/{(z,z⁻¹)}, M₁≅GSp₄, M₁₃≅GL₂×GL₁. Their moduli are |det|², |det α det β|⁵ and |ν|³ respectively.
hypotheses: The algebraic construction is over a characteristic-zero field unless a complex dual group is specified; orbit statements use the split octonion algebra. Local absolute values and smooth modules refer to the fixed p-adic convention.
proofSteps: Compute the wedge-cubic and unit stabilizers; determine Levi weights on radicals using the actual quotient torus. On V₄ identify the M₂ action as x↦αx βᵗ with multiplier det α det β.
acceptance: Scalar z on V acts on ∧²V by z² and ν⁻¹ by z⁻², so the action descends to PGSp₆.

The node uses the ν⁻¹ twist and similitude corrections of packet E10.

nodes.title: The PGSp₆ Weyl chamber
nodes.statement: On the M₃ torus, simple coroots are (1,t,t⁻¹),(t,t⁻¹,1),(1,t,t). On real characters s=(s₁,s₂,s₃), the third simple reflection is (s₁+s₂+s₃,−s₃,−s₂); the other two permute adjacent coordinates. The invariant quadratic form on characters is Σsᵢ²+(Σsᵢ)². The nine root hyperplanes are sᵢ−sⱼ=0 (i<j), sᵢ+sⱼ=0 (i<j), and sᵢ+Σsⱼ=0 (i=1,2,3); the positive chamber is s₁>s₂>|s₃|.
hypotheses: The algebraic construction is over a characteristic-zero field unless a complex dual group is specified; orbit statements use the split octonion algebra. Local absolute values and smooth modules refer to the fixed p-adic convention.
proofSteps: Generate all coroots from the three displayed simple coroots under their reflections; distinguish characters from cocharacters and verify the quadratic form by substitution.
acceptance: Check all nine hyperplanes, including 2s₁+s₂+s₃=0, and invariance under the third reflection.

nodes.title: P-series with supercuspidal inducing data
nodes.statement: For unitary supercuspidal τ of GL₂ and real s, I_P(s,τ) reduces precisely when τ≅τ∨ and either ωτ=1, s=±1/2, or ωτ≠1, s=0. At +1/2 there is a nonsplit sequence δP(τ)→I_P→JP with δP generic discrete series. At 0 the two constituents are a direct sum, exactly one generic.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Compute the normalized rank-one intertwiner and its Plancherel scalar on the two dual-radical representations; identify the generic constituent using Whittaker exactness. Negative points follow by duality.
acceptance: The negative point −1/2 must not be omitted; a nonselfdual τ has no reducibility point.

sources.match: GS lists the reducibility of P-induction from unitary supercuspidal GL₂ data: only for self-dual τ, at s = 1/2 with a nonsplit sequence whose submodule is a generic discrete series when the central character is trivial, and at s = 0 as a generic plus nongeneric sum otherwise. The source omits the point −1/2, which the node includes (packet E2).

nodes.title: P-series with Steinberg inducing data
nodes.statement: For τ=st⊗χ∘det and unitary χ, reducibility occurs only as follows: χ=1 at s=±3/2,±1/2; nontrivial χ²=1 or χ³=1 at s=±1/2. At +3/2 for χ=1 the submodule is St_G and quotient JP(3/2,st). At +1/2 for χ=1 the length-three series has bottom πgen[1], middle JQ(1/2,st), top JP(1/2,st). For nontrivial quadratic or cubic χ the length-two sequence has bottom generic discrete series πgen[χ] and top JP(1/2,stχ); cubic inversion gives πgen[χ]=πgen[χ⁻¹].
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Resolve the GL₂ Steinberg segment in its principal series, use induction in stages and compare normalized intertwining operators and Jacquet exponents.
acceptance: At χ=1,s=1/2 the length is 3, not 2; the cubic DS label is invariant under χ↦χ⁻¹.

sources.match: GS gives the reducibility points and composition series of P-induction from twisted Steinberg data: the Steinberg submodule at 3/2, length three at 1/2 for trivial twist, and generic discrete-series submodules for nontrivial quadratic and cubic twists.

nodes.title: P-series with one-dimensional inducing data
nodes.statement: For unitary χ, I_P(s,χ∘det) is reducible only at χ=1,s=±3/2,±1/2 and nontrivial χ²=1 or χ³=1,s=±1/2. At +3/2 the sequence is JQ(5/2,st)→I_P→1. Here π(a,b) denotes normalized GL₂ principal series, and negative parameters are dual statements.

nodes.title: Q-series with supercuspidal inducing data
nodes.statement: For unitary supercuspidal τ, I_Q(s,τ) reduces precisely when τ≅τ∨ and one of: ωτ=1,s=±1/2; ωτ≠1 with im φτ≅S₃,s=±1; ωτ≠1 with im φτ not S₃,s=0. At positive nonzero s it has generic discrete-series submodule δQ(τ) or πgen[τ] respectively, and Langlands quotient JQ. At 0 it is the direct sum of generic and nongeneric irreducibles.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Evaluate the standard and symmetric-cube factors in the dual Q radical, distinguish the S₃ dihedral parameter, and apply the rank-one reducibility criterion.
acceptance: The S₃ point is 1, unlike the determinant-trivial point 1/2.

sources.match: GS lists the reducibility of Q-induction from unitary supercuspidal data: ±1/2 for trivial central character, ±1 when the parameter has image S₃, and 0 otherwise for self-dual τ, with generic discrete-series submodules at the nonzero points.

nodes.title: Q-series with Steinberg or character data
nodes.statement: For stχ, reducibility occurs at χ=1,s=±5/2,±1/2 and nontrivial quadratic χ,s=±1/2. At χ=1,+5/2 the bottom is St_G; at +1/2 the bottom is πgen[1]⊕πdeg[1] and top JQ(1/2,st). For quadratic χ the bottom is πgen[χ] and top JQ(1/2,stχ). For χ∘det the same χ,s list applies: at χ=1,+5/2 the sequence is JP(3/2,st)→I_Q→1; at χ=1,+1/2 the length-three bottom, middle and top are JQ(1/2,st), JP(1/2,st), JQ(1,π(1,1)); for quadratic χ the sequence is JP(1/2,stχ)→I_Q→JQ(1,π(1,χ)).
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Compare Borel induction in stages through P and Q and use the segment resolution; determine submodule versus quotient using positive normalized exponents.
acceptance: The Q-induced st at 1/2 has two discrete-series submodules; its character-induced counterpart does not.

sources.match: GS gives the composition series of Q-induction from twisted Steinberg and from characters, including the two discrete-series submodules at 1/2 for the Steinberg case and the length-three series for the trivial character; the node uses the corrected quotient exponent for quadratic χ (packet E2).

nodes.title: Borel series and opposite embeddings
nodes.statement: Write χᵢ for the character values on the three long coroots with χ₁χ₂χ₃=1. Borel induction is irreducible unless some χᵢ=|·|^±1, some χᵢ/χⱼ=|·|^±1, or χ₁,χ₂,χ₃ are the three distinct nontrivial quadratics. In the last case it is generic⊕nongeneric. A Langlands quotient attached to exponents s₁≥s₂≥0 embeds in the opposite principal series; if χ₁=χ₂ and s₁=s₂+1≥1 its smaller P embedding is I_P(−s₁+1/2,χ₁⁻¹).
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Use the coroot criterion and the rank-two R-group; take the contragredient of the defining Langlands quotient and the one-dimensional GL₂ submodule in the exceptional embedding.
acceptance: The exceptional quadratic triple splits; the formula contains s₁, not an unbound s.

sources.match: GS embeds a Borel Langlands quotient into the opposite principal series, identifies the exceptional P-embedding when the two exponents differ by one, and states the irreducibility criterion for Borel induction in terms of the three long-coroot characters, with the generic plus nongeneric splitting for three distinct quadratic characters. The node uses s₁ in the exceptional embedding (packet E2).

nodes.title: Nontempered G₂ normal forms
nodes.statement: Every nontempered irreducible G₂ representation is uniquely a standard quotient of one of three disjoint normalized families: JQ(τ), with τ a positive unramified twist of tempered GL₂; JP(τ) with the same condition; or JP(τ) where τ is the GL₂ quotient of χ₁×χ₂, |χᵢ|=|·|^sᵢ and s₁>s₂>0. The first two families have positive central real exponent; the third uses the stated strictly ordered Borel chamber.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Specialize the general Langlands classification to the two maximal parabolics and Borel; translate Borel dominance through the chosen torus coordinates.
acceptance: Boundary s₂=0 belongs to a tempered-Levi family, not the third family.

sources.match: GS enumerates the irreducible nontempered representations of G₂ as the unique quotients of three families of induced representations: from Q and from P with positive twists of tempered GL₂ data, and from P with the quotient of a strictly ordered pair of characters.

nodes.title: Unipotent depth-zero supercuspidals
nodes.statement: Construct the G₂ depth-zero supercuspidals denoted πsc[1], πsc[ω], πsc[ω²] from cuspidal unipotent representations of the reductive quotient at a hyperspecial vertex and compact induction. Identify their Hecke eigenvalues and distinguish the three labels; the two nontrivial cubic labels are an unordered pair until an eigenvalue convention is chosen. Supply the exceptional finite-field character calculations needed to connect these labels with the subregular packet.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Use the parahoric quotient and cuspidal type criterion, compute the three unipotent cuspidal characters, and lift their matrix coefficients. Residue-characteristic restrictions of any finite-field calculation must be checked individually.
acceptance: Do not identify πsc[1] with the two nontrivial-cubic lifts or silently choose an ordering of ω,ω².

sources.match: GS describes π_sc[1], π_sc[ω] and π_sc[ω²] as depth-zero supercuspidals induced from cuspidal unipotent representations of G₂(F_q) inflated to a hyperspecial subgroup, and Proposition 7.1(iii) identifies the lifts of the nontrivial unramified cubic characters with the latter two. The node keeps the two cubic labels unordered (packet E9).

nodes.title: The parameter labels needed by theta
nodes.statement: Record only the established labels used here: Levi parameters for noncuspidal series; nondiscrete tempered packets of size one or two with unique generic member; principal-SL₂ Steinberg; subregular component group S₃ with πgen[1],πdeg[1],πsc[1]; and the quadratic/cubic or dihedral labels of the reducibility nodes. A discrete parameter trivial on the Deligne SL₂ has only supercuspidal members. The completed bijection and all endoscopic identities for G₂ belong to LocalLanglandsCorrespondenceForG2, which consumes this roadmap and is never an input.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Compare the long/short-root centralizers with the explicitly constructed representations and the GL₂/GL₃ parameter maps; distinguish desiderata of a full LLC from identities actually used by the theta calculations.
acceptance: A conjectural full G₂ LLC is not used to prove its own theta input.

sources.match: GS explains how the local Langlands correspondences of the Levi factors assign parameters to nontempered and to tempered non-discrete representations, notes that the tempered packets have size one or two with a unique generic member, and lists the non-supercuspidal members of the discrete packets by the image of SL₂.

nodes.title: Finite cubic models for nongeneric G₂
nodes.statement: If π is irreducible, infinite-dimensional and nongeneric, W_E(π) is finite-dimensional for every cubic étale E and nonzero for at least one E. No such nonzero assertion is made for the trivial representation. The proof must include the nilpotent-wavefront reduction to the subregular orbit and the p-adic local character-expansion/degenerate-Whittaker comparison, including residual characteristic 2 and 3.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: For nongeneric infinite-dimensional G₂ representations, eliminate the regular wavefront orbit, show the maximal remaining orbit is subregular, and apply the multiplicity comparison to its rational cubic forms.
acceptance: The trivial representation is an excluded degenerate case; finite dimension is required before comparing period dimensions.

sources.match: GS states that a nongeneric infinite-dimensional irreducible representation has a nonzero, and always finite-dimensional, twisted Jacquet module along N for some cubic étale E, deducing it from the subregular support of the wave-front set and the results of Mœglin–Waldspurger and of Varma in residue characteristic 2, which it cites.

nodes.title: PGSp₆ P₂ and P₁₃ series
nodes.statement: For unitary supercuspidal τ of GL₂, I₂(s,τ⊗τ) has the same reducibility cases as I_Q(s,τ): determinant-trivial at ±1/2 with generic DS δ₂(τ), S₃ dihedral at ±1 with generic DS σgen[τ], and other selfdual determinant-nontrivial at 0 with generic⊕nongeneric splitting. For τ=stχ, I₂ reduces only for χ=1 at ±5/2,±1/2 and nontrivial quadratic χ at ±1/2. At +5/2 the bottom is St_H; at χ=1,+1/2 it is I₃(St)gen; at quadratic χ,+1/2 it is DS σgen[χ], always with standard quotient on top. I₁₃(s,τ⊗1) for supercuspidal τ reduces only for selfdual τ with ωτ=1,s=±1/2 (length four, unique generic DS submodule δ₁₃(τ)), or ωτ≠1,im φτ≠S₃,s=0 (two summands).
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Calculate the dual radical factors and rank-one intertwining scalars; resolve the Steinberg segment and compare Jacquet exponents. Keep the anti-diagonal central quotient on M₂ explicit.
acceptance: Length four at I₁₃(1/2,τ⊗1) is not replaced by a length-two sequence.

sources.match: GS gives the reducibility points and constituents of P₂-induction from τ⊗τ (supercuspidal and Steinberg τ) and of P₁₃-induction from τ⊗1 for supercuspidal τ, with the discrete-series constituents δ₂(τ), σ_gen[τ], σ_gen[χ] and δ₁₃(τ).

nodes.title: Siegel induction on PGSp₆
nodes.statement: For a GL₃ discrete-series τ with trivial central character, I₃(τ)=I₃(τ∨) is irreducible if τ is not selfdual; for selfdual τ it is the direct sum of generic and nongeneric tempered irreducibles. For GL₃ Borel series χ₁×χ₂×χ₃ with product 1 the irreducibility exceptions are χᵢ=|·|^±1 or χᵢ/χⱼ=|·|^±1 and the distinct nontrivial quadratic triple, in which last case I₃ is generic⊕nongeneric.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Compute the Siegel R-group and normalized intertwiners; compare Tadić’s classification with the GL₃/μ₂ coordinate convention.
acceptance: Selfdual discrete-series induction splits even though nonselfdual induction is irreducible.

sources.match: GS states that Siegel induction from a discrete-series GL₃ representation with trivial central character is irreducible unless τ is self-dual, when it splits as a generic plus a nongeneric summand, and gives the corresponding statements for Borel data.

nodes.title: P₁ reducibility including the nongeneric SK case
nodes.statement: Let τ be a supercuspidal representation of GSp₄ with trivial central character and parameter whose 5-dimensional standard composition contains 1. Then I₁(s,τ) reduces exactly at real s=±1/2 and at +1/2 has DS submodule δ₁(τ) and Langlands quotient J₁(1/2,τ). Prove this first for generic τ, then prove it for the nongeneric Saito–Kurokawa τρ used in EX.8. The latter is a separate obligation: Shahidi’s generic theorem alone does not imply it.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: For generic τ compute the rank-one Plancherel measure of I₁(s, τ) from the standard and twisted factors of its parameter and apply the Harish-Chandra–Silberger criterion for reducibility of rank-one supercuspidal induction.

For the nongeneric τ_ρ use part (vi) of the Gan–Takeda correspondence (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions §3.5): the Plancherel measures of a nongeneric supercuspidal agree with those attached to its parameter, hence with those of the generic member of its packet; the same criterion then gives reducibility exactly at ±1/2. Shahidi’s generic local-coefficient theorem is not applied to τ_ρ directly.
Apply the square-integrability criterion to the submodule at +1/2.
acceptance: A proof accepting nongeneric τ directly into Shahidi’s generic local coefficient is rejected; the Plancherel comparison of Gan–Takeda (vi) is the route.

sources.locator: Proposition 10.4, p. 33; Proposition 15.6 and proof, pp. 54–55
sources.match: GS states that P₁-induction from a supercuspidal GSp₄ representation whose standard parameter contains 1 reduces exactly at ±1/2, with a discrete-series submodule δ₁(τ), and applies this to the nongeneric τ_ρ in Proposition 15.6. The node separates the nongeneric case, which GS justifies by generic reducibility theory (packet E11).

nodes.title: Freudenthal–Jordan exceptional data
nodes.statement: For J = F, a cubic étale algebra E, the Jordan algebra D⁺ of a degree-three central simple algebra D (or its split form M₃(F)⁺), or the 15-dimensional algebra H₃(B) of Hermitian 3 × 3 matrices over a quaternion algebra B, equip J with its cubic norm, adjoint and trace form; these cubic norm structures are constructed here. Form g_J = sl₃ ⊕ Lie(M_J) ⊕ (F³ ⊗ J) ⊕ (F³ ⊗ J)* with the Freudenthal bracket, and identify its type as G₂, D₄, E₆ or E₇ for dim J = 1, 3, 9, 15, compatibly with the split exceptional Lie algebras of LieHighestWeight Layer 8; the embedded g₂ is sl₃ ⊕ (F³ ⊗ 1_J) ⊕ (F³ ⊗ 1_J)*.
hypotheses: The algebraic construction is over a characteristic-zero field unless a complex dual group is specified; orbit statements use the split octonion algebra. Local absolute values and smooth modules refer to the fixed p-adic convention.
proofSteps: Construct the cubic norm, adjoint and trace of each J from the norm of E, the reduced norm of D and the quaternion norm of B, and check the Jordan adjoint identities.

Define the bracket on g_J, verify the Jacobi identity from those identities, and compare root systems and dimensions with the LieHighestWeight Layer 8 models after extending scalars to an algebraic closure.
acceptance: An arbitrary cubic polynomial without the Jordan adjoint identities is not admissible input.

sources.match: GS attaches to a Freudenthal–Jordan algebra J the Lie algebra sl₃ ⊕ Lie(M_J) ⊕ (F³⊗J) ⊕ (F³⊗J)* of type G₂, D₄, E₆ or E₇ for dim J = 1, 3, 9, 15, describes J in each case (cubic étale, 9-dimensional from a central simple algebra with involution of the second kind, Hermitian 3×3 matrices over a quaternion algebra), and identifies the centralizer of Aut(J) with the J = F algebra g₂ (with the dual summand of packet E3).

nodes.title: The three exceptional group dual pairs
nodes.statement: Integrate the commuting Lie embeddings to G₂×HJ in the adjoint group GJ, and identify their mutual centralizers. For J=D⁺, HJ(F)=PD×; for J=M₃⁺, HJ=PGL₃⋊C₂ in E₆⋊C₂; for the 15-dimensional J, HJ=PGSp₆ in E₇. Construct the E₆ form attached to either cubic division algebra and the chosen split G₂ subgroup. Group embeddings and central quotients are part of this target, not consequences assumed from a Lie inclusion alone.
hypotheses: The algebraic construction is over a characteristic-zero field unless a complex dual group is specified; orbit statements use the split octonion algebra. Local absolute values and smooth modules refer to the fixed p-adic convention.
proofSteps: Use root group integration, Jordan descent and the lattice maps of the adjoint forms; verify centralizers after algebraic closure and descend them.
acceptance: For a division D, an outer automorphism of geometric E₆ does not automatically provide an F-rational outer automorphism of D.

sources.match: GS forms the dual pairs G₂ × Aut(J) in Aut(G_J), notes the disconnected Aut(J) when dim J = 9, and tabulates H_J = PD×, PGL₃ ⋊ Z/2Z and PGSp₆ for the three J used.

nodes.title: Cubic triality and the exceptional see-saw
nodes.statement: A cubic étale E with its permutation Galois action on three embeddings defines the trialitarian Spin₈^E. For an embedding i:E→J construct HJ,E=Aut(i) and the commuting pair HJ,E×Spin₈^E inside GJ. Identify HJ,E as PE× for division D, PE×⋊C₂ for M₃, and the algebraic quotient Res_E/F SL₂/μ₂ for J of dimension 15. The resulting square with G₂×HJ gives the see-saw on the same minimal representation. Do not replace rational points of a central quotient by a quotient of rational points without checking its H¹ obstruction.
hypotheses: The algebraic construction is over a characteristic-zero field unless a complex dual group is specified; orbit statements use the split octonion algebra. Local absolute values and smooth modules refer to the fixed p-adic convention.
proofSteps: Descend the pinned D₄ triality action along the étale S₃ torsor; compute centralizers of E and match the two restrictions of GJ.
acceptance: For E=F³ recover split Spin₈; for E a cubic field the division centralizer is the anisotropic torus PE×.

sources.match: GS fixes an embedding of a cubic étale algebra E in J, forms Aut(i: E → J) commuting with the quasi-split Spin₈ attached to E, draws the see-saw with G₂ × Aut(J), and tabulates the groups H_{J,E} for the three J. The node uses Spin₈^E for the misprinted group symbol (packet E3).

nodes.title: Local minimal representations
nodes.statement: Construct the nonzero irreducible unitarizable minimal representations ΠJ of the required split D/E groups and E₆^D forms, with their chosen central character. For split simply-laced groups select the spherical representation with the subregular-dual Satake parameter and prove its minimality; for E₆^D construct the smooth model of Savin §3. Supply Schrödinger/rank-one models, the exact evaluation-at-zero sequence and ambient-radical Jacquet action needed below. Existence, irreducibility, unitarity and model comparison are proof targets, not axioms on a user-supplied representation.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Build each smooth model and its intertwining operators from the highest-weight orbit; prove the Weyl relations, irreducibility and the unitary completion, then compare normalized Jacquet exponents.
acceptance: The model is a constructed representation, rather than an arbitrary representation declared to satisfy desired Jacquet formulas.

sources.match: GS restricts the minimal representation of the adjoint exceptional group (cited from Gan–Savin 2005) to the three dual pairs and uses its Jacquet modules throughout.
Savin constructs the minimal representation of the E₆ form attached to a cubic division algebra and records, after Rumelhart, that it is minimal.
Gan–Savin 2004 recall the minimal representation of split E₆ used for the pair PGL₃ × G₂.

Magaard–Savin give, for the minimal representation of a group of type D, E₆ or E₇ and a maximal parabolic with commutative unipotent radical N, an exact sequence with the compactly supported functions on the open orbit as submodule and the N-coinvariants, a twisted minimal representation of the Levi plus a character, as quotient.

Orbit kernels and twisted coefficients require compatible concrete realizations.

nodes.title: Exceptional big and small theta modules
nodes.statement: Specialize the imported commuting-action theta construction to ΠJ. For irreducible π of G₂, the maximal π-isotypic quotient is π⊗ΘJ(π), equivalently the appropriate smooth coinvariant model with π∨; use the same convention for HJ input. Define θJ(π) as the maximal semisimple quotient only once finite length is proved. Use full algebraic duals in Hom descriptions and smooth contragredients only where admissibility justifies them.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Apply the universal isotypic quotient to the commuting exceptional actions and prove the exceptional see-saw by the two Hom adjunctions on ΠJ; no classical oscillator Howe theorem is asserted for this restriction.
acceptance: A nonzero big module need not be declared irreducible before the finite-length and uniqueness targets.

Relate successive period spaces on both sides.

nodes.title: The spherical extension across the E₆ involution
nodes.statement: Extend the split E₆ minimal representation to E₆⋊C₂ by requiring the pinned involution to fix its spherical vector. On PGL₃ the involution is g↦w₀(gᵗ)⁻¹w₀⁻¹ with antidiagonal entries (1,−1,1); it fixes G₂ pointwise. Prove its square is 1 on Π and compatibility with the orbit model, not only invariance of its isomorphism class.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Normalize the intertwiner by the spherical vector and then evaluate it on the explicit model to determine the stabilizer characters on coefficient orbits.
acceptance: Changing the extension by the sign character interchanges plus/minus labels and is detected by the Whittaker coefficient.

nodes.title: Ambient E₆/E₇ gradings
nodes.statement: The two fundamental G₂ cocharacters define E₇ parabolics with derived Levi types D₆ and A₁A₅. The three PGSp₆ cocharacters define ambient derived Levi types E₆,D₆,A₁D₅ for P₃,P₁,P₂ respectively. Construct their intersections with both dual-pair factors, opposite radicals, central characters and projections Π_Nsmall→Π_𝒩ambient. In every top-piece formula it is the ambient-radical quotient Π_𝒩 that occurs, not a second copy of the small-radical quotient.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Compute all weights of the Freudenthal bracket under each cocharacter and group the positive weights; compare the zero-weight subgroup and its central lattice.
acceptance: Verify the five derived Levi types and the inclusions of small radicals into ambient radicals.

sources.match: GS obtains parabolics of E₇ from the fundamental cocharacters of G₂ with Levi types D₆ and A₁ × A₅, and from those of PGSp₆ maximal parabolics with Levi types D₆, A₁ × D₅ and E₆.

nodes.title: Rank-one and rank-two octonion orbit kernels
nodes.statement: Identify the kernels of the small-to-ambient Jacquet projections with compact-function modules on highest-weight orbit intersections. For P₁ the null octonion quadruples x,x′,y,y′ satisfy all pairwise products zero and x∧x′+y∧y′=0, giving strata of span dimension 1 and 2. For P₂ impose dependent spinor columns as well as trace zero, then compute the two span strata. Determine stabilizers and modular-density actions separately on each stratum; no single unknown character is assumed to normalize both.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Use the half-spin highest-weight equations and the null-space classification. Compute the tangent action on each stabilizer quotient to determine its density character before applying normalized induction.
acceptance: The split P₂ calculation contains an extra middle piece; omitting it gives the nonsplit answer.

sources.match: GS describes the kernel of the projection to the ambient Jacquet module by null octonion quadruples with x ∧ x′ + y ∧ y′ = 0, splits them by span dimension, and for P₂ introduces an undetermined twist δ′; the node computes each stratum separately (packet E15).

nodes.title: Raw E₆ Jacquet input and noncuspidal finiteness
nodes.statement: Construct the two outer-related PGL₃ maximal-parabolic Jacquet filtrations of Π_E6 with bottom regular GL₂ piece, middle regular GL₁ piece, and top D₅-minimal plus trivial pieces, and the G₂-P filtration with two GL₂ regular pieces, a GL₁ piece and A₅-minimal plus trivial top. In GS04 notation P₂=our P and P₁=our Q; retain its normalized determinant factors. Deduce finite length of the noncuspidal part of every theta lift in either direction without invoking full E₆ Howe duality.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: For PGL₃→G₂, normalize the bottom and middle terms by |det|^(3/2), the top by |det|^(1/2)Π_D5⊕|det|^(3/2). For G₂-P, use |det|^(1/2) on both regular strata and Π_A5⊕|det|^(1/2) on top.

nodes.title: The generic supercuspidal precursor

A generic supercuspidal σ of PGSp₆ has a nonzero G₂ lift exactly when it has a Shalika functional, and that lift is irreducible, generic and supercuspidal. nodes.title: Howe duality for split E₆
nodes.statement: For H₃×G₂ the big lifts in both directions have finite length, each nonzero small lift is irreducible, and distinct inputs have distinct nonzero small lifts. The image on H₃ is exactly the extensions listed in the E₆ table. Tempered and discrete-series representations are preserved on nonzero lifts. nodes.title: The enhanced Fourier–Jacobi period

The oscillator representation ρψ of U/Z extends to Mp₂⋉U; for a genuine Mp₂ module Iψ(s) form I_conjugateψ(s)⊗ρψ, whose two genuine signs cancel so it descends to J. Define its Fourier–Jacobi period on π by Hom_J(π,I_conjugateψ(s)⊗ρψ), with the normalized genuine principal series and the stated additive-character convention.

For each smooth vector prove compact support of the integrand modulo the relevant stabilizer; integration of an arbitrary constant along a whole noncompact root group is not defined.

sources.match: GS forms the chain of Whittaker, Shalika and Fourier–Jacobi period spaces for a tempered pair π ⊗ τ in the minimal representation and shows they are all one-dimensional when π is generic, using Propositions 11.5 and 11.7 and Lemma 11.3 at s = −1/2.

nodes.title: Uniqueness for generic tempered quotients
nodes.statement: For tempered τ of H, ΘG₂(τ) has at most one tempered generic irreducible quotient. For tempered generic π of G₂, ΘH(π) has a unique irreducible quotient, which has the genericity specified by the explicit lift table. Multiplicity is one and the resulting assignment is injective on these nonzero lifts.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: If two generic quotients occur, their independent Whittaker lines contradict the one-dimensional period chain; treat supercuspidal quotients through the earlier precursor and noncuspidal quotients through finite-length Jacquet support.
acceptance: The uniqueness proof must bound the supercuspidal part as well as the noncuspidal part.

sources.locator: Propositions 12.2–12.3 and the remark after 12.2, p. 39
sources.match: GS deduces that Θ(τ) for tempered τ cannot have two tempered generic irreducible quotients and that Θ(π) for tempered generic π cannot have two tempered irreducible quotients; the remark attributing the result to Savin–Weissman is limited to supercuspidal τ (packet E14).

nodes.title: Tempered Howe duality in E₇
nodes.statement: For every tempered irreducible on either side of G₂×H, the big theta lift has finite length and zero or irreducible maximal semisimple quotient, with multiplicity one; two inputs cannot have the same nonzero small lift. The nonzero lifts are tempered. Combine generic period uniqueness and nongeneric cubic uniqueness, and include generic/noncuspidal and nongeneric/supercuspidal mixed possibilities.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Use compact-center supercuspidal splitting and the two independent period bounds to bound the full big module. Distinguish generic and nongeneric quotients with the raw Whittaker fiber; apply reciprocity to obtain injectivity.
acceptance: Neither an unproved finite-length hypothesis nor a classical oscillator Howe theorem can replace the exceptional argument.

sources.match: GS concludes Howe duality for tempered representations of G₂ in G₂ × PGSp₆ (finite length, unique tempered quotient, injectivity) from the uniqueness results and the noncuspidal finiteness of §14; the node also records the PGSp₆ side.

nodes.title: Explicit nontempered lifts
nodes.statement: If π=JQ(τ), then θH(π)=J₂(τ⊗τ); if π=JP(τ) in either allowed P family, θH(π)=J₁₃(τ⊗1). These big lifts have finite length. Conversely these are exactly the nontempered H representations with nonzero G₂ lift. Under the fixed GL₂ LLC and exceptional dual-group embedding, the two parameters match.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: The positive-exponent comparison identifies the full module as a quotient of a finite-length induction, so its Langlands quotient is unique. Read its dual-Levi parameter through the fixed lattice coordinates.
acceptance: Use positive real exponents and the correct P₁₃/P₂ Levi conventions, including the character-induction P cases.

sources.match: GS determines the lifts of nontempered representations: J_Q(τ) ↦ J₂(τ⊗τ) and J_P(τ) ↦ J₁₃(τ⊗1), with finite-length big lifts, and these are the only nontempered PGSp₆ representations with nonzero lift.

nodes.title: Howe duality for all three exceptional pairs
nodes.statement: For each of PD××G₂, H₃×G₂ and G₂×H, every irreducible input has a finite-length big theta lift and zero or irreducible small theta lift; the nonzero small assignment is injective. Irr♣, the G₂ domain of the H₃ correspondence, is contained in Irr♥. PD× nonzero lifts are discrete series, H₃ lifts preserve temperedness and discreteness, and H lifts preserve temperedness. PD× is fully hit when p≠3.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Combine the three independent proofs and nontempered classification; use the explicitly computed E₆-to-E₇ table to prove Irr♣⊂Irr♥ rather than regard three nonzero domains as disjoint.
acceptance: This does not assert surjectivity onto Irr(H), and it does not assert PD× surjectivity at p=3.

sources.locator: Theorems 1.2–1.3, pp. 2–3; Theorem 7.2, p. 23; Theorem 8.5, p. 27; Theorem 15.1, p. 52
sources.match: GS states Howe duality for the three dual pairs, the preservation of temperedness and the inclusion of the PGL₃ domain in the PGSp₆ domain, and the injection of Irr(PD×) for p ≠ 3.
Gan–Savin restate these results as the input of the local Langlands correspondence for G₂.

nodes.title: The E₆-to-E₇ tempered Siegel table
nodes.statement: For tempered τ of PGL₃ and π=θM₃(τ±) nonzero, θH(π) is I₃(τ) if τ is nonselfdual or if its selfdual parameter contains 1. In the remaining selfdual cases, θH(θM₃(τ+))=I₃(τ)gen and θH(θM₃(τ−))=I₃(τ)deg. In the contains-1 case I₃(τ) is irreducible by the applicable non-discrete-series criterion; do not apply the discrete-series splitting rule outside its hypothesis.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Use the P₃ Jacquet top E₆ term to produce the quotient, compare genericity and finite length, then use the PGSp₆ reducibility table to distinguish the two signs.
acceptance: The parameter-contains-1 case has only the plus E₆ lift; it is not a two-sign splitting.

sources.match: GS gives the PGSp₆ lifts of the tempered lifts from PGL₃: the irreducible Siegel induction I₃(τ) for nonself-dual τ and for self-dual parameters containing 1, and the generic and nongeneric summands of I₃(τ) for the other self-dual cases.

nodes.title: The remaining tempered non-supercuspidal lifts
nodes.statement: For unitary discrete-series GL₂ τ, θH(IQ(τ))=I₂(τ⊗τ), matching generic/degenerate summands where these split; θH(δQ(τ))=δ₂(τ) when ωτ=1; θH(δP(τ))=δ₁₃(τ) in the selfdual determinant-trivial case. The S₃-dihedral, nontrivial quadratic and Steinberg entries are πgen[τ]↦σgen[τ], πgen[χ]↦σgen[χ], and StG₂↦StH. Together with the E₆ table and πdeg[1] on the division side this covers every tempered non-supercuspidal π.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Construct maps using the two G₂ Jacquet bottom pieces and follow their discrete-series submodules under the known reducibility filtrations; use genericity to select the correct member.
acceptance: Both supercuspidal and Steinberg-twist GL₂ input families, including the exceptional quadratic entries, are accounted for.

sources.match: GS lists the lifts of the remaining tempered non-supercuspidal representations: I_Q(τ) ↦ I₂(τ⊗τ) with matching summands, δ_Q(τ) ↦ δ₂(τ), δ_P(τ) ↦ δ₁₃(τ), π_gen[τ] ↦ σ_gen[τ], π_gen[χ] ↦ σ_gen[χ] and Steinberg to Steinberg (packet E18 for the missing derivations).

nodes.title: The nongeneric πρ family
nodes.statement: For a supercuspidal ρ of PGL₂ let σρ be its classical theta lift on Mp₂ through the anisotropic ternary group using JL(ρ). Its mixed Mp₂×G₂ lift πρ is irreducible nongeneric supercuspidal and determines ρ. These πρ exhaust the supercuspidals outside the PD× and PGL₃ images which have a nonzero reverse Mp₂ mixed lift. The odd-Weil case is excluded by this ternary-first-occurrence construction.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Use the imported division-ternary theta theorem and the mixed-module first-occurrence criterion, then recover σρ from the Fourier–Jacobi module and ρ from the classical inverse correspondence.

Nonvanishing, irreducibility and injectivity of σ ↦ θ(σ) on genuine supercuspidals are MetaplecticAutomorphicForms §3.38a; this node adds the description of the family π_ρ and its exhaustion property (GS Lemma 15.4(iii)).
acceptance: Do not infer irreducibility for the excluded odd Weil module from the supercuspidal case.

sources.match: GS defines σ_ρ as the metaplectic lift of the Jacquet–Langlands transfer of ρ to the anisotropic PB× and π_ρ as its lift to G₂, and recalls from Gan–Gurevich that π_ρ is irreducible supercuspidal, that ρ ↦ π_ρ is injective, and that these exhaust the supercuspidals lifting to the metaplectic SL₂ but not from PGL₃ or PD×. The node reads "anisotropic" for the misprinted "isotropic" (packet E6).
Gan–Gurevich give the nongenericity of these lifts.

nodes.title: The πρ lift to the D₆ factor
nodes.statement: Let τρ be the nongeneric supercuspidal Saito–Kurokawa representation of PGSp₄ attached by classical theta to σρ. Then Θ_D6(πρ)=τρ under the orthogonal-minimal comparison. Specify the same additive character and dual convention throughout.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Use the orthogonal-minimal see-saw comparison with full algebraic duals; the classical rank-one theta result identifies the only nonzero quotient and its multiplicity.
acceptance: An equality of semisimplified small modules is not silently promoted to equality of big modules.

sources.locator: Lemma 15.4 (definition of τ_ρ) and Lemma 15.5 with proof, p. 54
sources.match: GS defines τ_ρ as the lift of σ_ρ to SO₅, a nongeneric supercuspidal in a Saito–Kurokawa packet, and proves through the see-saw (14.3) that the SO₁₂-minimal lift of π_ρ to SO₅ is τ_ρ.

nodes.title: The remaining PGSp₆ supercuspidal-input table
nodes.statement: For the πρ family, θH(πρ)=δ₁(τρ), the discrete-series submodule of I₁(1/2,τρ). For every other supercuspidal π of G₂ outside the division and split-E₆ images, θH(π) is supercuspidal. For generic such π the lift is generic supercuspidal. Include p=2,3 in the local theta theorem, while preserving any source-specific restrictions on the separate depth-zero examples.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Analyze every proper H Jacquet module of the supercuspidal input using the raw filtrations; only the D₆ top term can survive, and the comparison identifies exactly the πρ family. Use nongeneric SK reducibility to select δ₁(τρ).
acceptance: The nongeneric rank-one Plancherel calculation is a named unresolved obligation, not an application of the generic Shahidi theorem.

sources.match: GS shows that for supercuspidal π not lifted from PGL₃ or PD× the PGSp₆ lift is the discrete-series submodule δ₁(τ_ρ) of I₁(1/2, τ_ρ) when π = π_ρ and is supercuspidal otherwise, using the P₁ Jacquet filtration and Lemma 15.5.

nodes.title: The discrete-series trichotomy
nodes.statement: Every discrete-series representation of G₂ has a nonzero discrete-series theta lift to exactly one of PD×, H₃ and PGSp₆. The PD× and H₃ domains, and their complement inside the PGSp₆ domain, give the three subsets. Whenever θH(π) is discrete series, it is generic exactly when π is generic. A representation in the H₃ branch can also have a nonzero H lift, but that H lift is not discrete series.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Read discreteness and genericity from every explicit table entry and the supercuspidal classification.
acceptance: The three alternatives count discrete-series target lifts, not all nonzero lifts to all three groups.

sources.match: GS states that every discrete series of G₂ lifts to a discrete series of exactly one of PD×, PGL₃ ⋊ Z/2Z and PGSp₆, the PGSp₆ lift being generic exactly when π is (packet E6 for the group name).
Gan–Savin restate the trichotomy and use the generic discrete-series lifts to PGSp₆ in their spin-lifting argument.

nodes.title: The supercuspidal spin-pole criterion
nodes.statement: For generic supercuspidal σ of PGSp₆, the following are equivalent: a nonzero Shalika functional; a nonzero exceptional lift to G₂; a pole at s=0 of the Shahidi degree-eight spin L-factor. In this event its G₂ lift is irreducible generic supercuspidal. The generic G₂ supercuspidal dichotomy is the precursor already imported in EX.5.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Combine the supercuspidal theta–Shalika calculation with the Langlands–Shahidi local coefficient pole calculation, after fixing the Spin₇ eight-dimensional spin representation.
acceptance: Only Shahidi’s supercuspidal generic factor is used; do not replace it with an unconstructed G₂ LLC factor.

sources.match: Savin–Weissman prove that a generic supercuspidal σ of PGSp₆ with trivial central character lifts to G₂ exactly when it has a Shalika functional, the lift then being generic supercuspidal, and that the Shalika functional exists exactly when the spin L-function of σ has a pole at s = 0.

nodes.title: A generic depth-zero lift example
nodes.statement: Construct the specific generic depth-zero supercuspidal G₂ representations used in LL §§8.4 and 10.3 whose H lifts are supercuspidal; relate their finite-reductive cuspidal type and first-occurrence calculation. Record the precise residue-field and regular-character conditions of the finite-group calculation before using this as a local globalization input.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Pass from a regular finite-group cuspidal type to compact induction, compute its exceptional first occurrence and use generic supercuspidal injectivity to identify the H lift.
acceptance: This example is a target with a finite-group source-verification gap; the p≥5 hypothesis of the different GS04 example cannot supply an all-primes theorem.

sources.match: Gan–Savin use generic depth-zero supercuspidals of G₂ whose lifts to PGSp₆ are generic supercuspidal, citing Gan's exceptional correspondence over finite fields for their existence.
Gan–Savin 2004 give a separate depth-zero example under p ≥ 5, which does not supply the representations used here (gap G5).

nodes.title: Quaternion pointwise stabilizers
nodes.statement: For a characteristic-zero local field and an octonion algebra O, let D⊂O be a quaternion subalgebra. Define GD as its pointwise stabilizer in Aut(O); the Cayley–Dickson decomposition identifies GD with SL₁(D). All embeddings of a fixed D in O are conjugate. Its setwise stabilizer is the larger SO₄ form; never use that group in place of GD.
hypotheses: F is a characteristic-zero local field, including R; O is an octonion algebra over F and D⊂O a quaternion algebra.
proofSteps: Use O=D⊕D·u with its Cayley–Dickson multiplication to calculate automorphisms fixing D pointwise; apply the extension theorem for quaternion embeddings.
acceptance: D is quaternion here; it is unrelated to the degree-three division algebra of EX.5.

sources.match: Gan–Savin take the pointwise stabilizer G_D of a quaternion subalgebra D of the octonions and identify it with the norm-one group of D.

api.statement: GD≅SL₁(D), with its action on D⊥ given by the norm-one parameter in Cayley–Dickson coordinates.

api.name: quaternion_stabilizer_conjugate

api.name: quaternion_stabilizer_setwise

tests.statement: For D=M₂(F), GD≅SL₂(F), which is noncompact for nonarchimedean F.

tests.name: quaternionStabilizer_division_compact
tests.statement: For division D over a nonarchimedean F, GD is compact.

tests.name: quaternionStabilizer_real
tests.statement: For the real division octonions and D=Hamilton quaternions, GD is SU₂, not SO₄.

uses.how: Produce local relative models for the period globalization input.
Unfold the global GD period in the exceptional theta integral.

nodes.title: Siegel character orbits and quaternion coefficients
nodes.statement: For H=PGSp₆, the open orbits of its Siegel Levi M₃ on the character space of N₃ are indexed by quaternion F-algebras D. The stabilizer of a representative ψD is Aut(D). For Π_E7 restricted to Aut(O)×H, Π_(N₃,ψD)=c-Ind_GD^Aut(O)1 when D embeds in O and is zero otherwise.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Classify nondegenerate ternary symmetric forms up to the actual M₃ similitude action and identify their even Clifford quaternion algebra.
In the rank-one Albert model identify the ψD fiber with embeddings of D in O; use the pointwise stabilizer, not Aut(D), on the G₂ side.
acceptance: The Levi stabilizer and the G₂ coefficient stabilizer are different groups.

sources.match: Gan–Savin state that the Siegel Levi of PGSp₆ has open orbits on characters of the Siegel radical indexed by quaternion algebras D, with stabilizer Aut(D), and that the corresponding twisted Jacquet module of the E₇ minimal representation is compactly induced from G_D (packet E19 for the omitted orbit label).

sources.locator: Chapter 5, §3, Lemma 3.4 and case (4) of its proof, pp. 197–198
sources.match: Gross–Savin show that the rational points of G act transitively on the rank-one elements of the relevant type with stabilizer the norm-one group of D; Gan–Savin cite case (4) of the proof for the local identification of the twisted Jacquet module with compact induction from G_D.

nodes.title: Tempered lifts have quaternion relative models
nodes.statement: If θH(π) is nonzero tempered, then for some quaternion D⊂O the representation π is a quotient of c-Ind_GD^G1. A tempered H representation has a nonzero full-rank Siegel coefficient: otherwise its restriction to Sp₆ has rank at most two and belongs to a classical O(m) theta image with m≤2, which is non-tempered.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Import the full low-rank unitary classification including ranks zero and one, obtain a nonzero open-orbit coefficient, then take the corresponding coefficient of the theta quotient and apply the explicit minimal fiber.
acceptance: The rank-at-most-two argument must not assume exact rank two.

sources.match: Gan–Savin prove that if θ(π) is tempered then π is a quotient of compact induction from G_D for some quaternion D, because a tempered PGSp₆ representation with no full-rank Siegel coefficient would have Howe N-rank at most two and come from a small orthogonal group by Li's classification (packet E20 for 'at most two').

sources.locator: Chapter 5, §3, Lemma 3.4 and case (4) of its proof, pp. 197–198
sources.match: The orbit and stabilizer computation that Gan–Savin cite for the twisted Jacquet module used in the proof.

nodes.title: Supercuspidal relative embeddings
nodes.statement: If π is supercuspidal with θH(π)≠0, then π embeds in c-Ind_GD^G1 for a suitable quaternion D⊂O. Tempered compatibility supplies the relative quotient and supercuspidal projectivity for the compact-center group splits it.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Use the quotient theorem and split in the relevant supercuspidal block; record the central-character category in which projectivity is used.
acceptance: This splitting does not claim projectivity for arbitrary discrete series.

sources.match: Gan–Savin deduce, by projectivity of supercuspidals, that a supercuspidal π with nonzero lift is a submodule of compact induction from G_D for some D.

nodes.title: The Steinberg relative discrete summand
nodes.statement: For split p-adic G₂ and division quaternion D, St_G₂ is a Hilbert direct summand of L²(GD∖G₂). Its H lift is St_H, whose restriction to a maximal unipotent has the required regular model; hence its ψD Siegel coefficient is nonzero. Since GD is compact, a GD-fixed vector and square-integrable matrix coefficients give the closed relative embedding.
hypotheses: Local convention: F is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero, coefficients are complex, and ψ is a fixed nontrivial unitary additive character, unless a different field is specified.
proofSteps: Import the precise Steinberg-unipotent regular restriction, obtain a nonzero GD period from the minimal coefficient, and realize the relative embedding by matrix coefficients; use square integrability and unitarity to split it.
acceptance: Compactness of GD is essential to the displayed Hilbert argument.

sources.match: Gan–Savin show that for a division quaternion D the Steinberg representation is a direct summand of L²(G_D∖G), using that its lift is the Steinberg representation of PGSp₆, the restriction of Steinberg to a maximal unipotent subgroup, and the anisotropy of G_D.

nodes.title: Every compact real G₂ representation has an SU₂ period
nodes.statement: For the compact real G₂ and a Hamilton quaternion subalgebra, every irreducible finite-dimensional representation has a nonzero GD≅SU₂-fixed vector and embeds in L²(GD∖G₂).
hypotheses: The field is R and O is the division octonion algebra.
proofSteps: Restrict to the compact long-root SU₃. For a highest weight λ₁≥λ₂≥λ₃, the U₂ interlacing weight (λ₂,λ₂) occurs; its restriction to SU₂ is trivial. Apply Peter–Weyl to the resulting fixed vector.
acceptance: This imports the algebraic/compact Gelfand–Tsetlin rule and is distinct from p-adic GL₃↓GL₂ generic restriction.

sources.match: Gan–Savin show that every irreducible representation of the compact real G₂ has nonzero vectors fixed by the stabilizer of the real quaternion division algebra, hence embeds in L² of the quotient, by branching through SU₃ and SU₂.

nodes.title: The global Albert E₇ pair
nodes.statement: For a number field k and octonion O/k, use the existing Albert algebra J₃(O) and Koecher–Tits construction to form the adjoint group E(O) of absolute type E₇, containing Aut(O)×PGSp₆. For totally real k and totally definite O it has k-rank 3 and compact G at every real place; for split O the ambient group is split E₇ of rank 7. Construct the global embeddings and their compatibility with every local model.
hypotheses: k is a number field; O/k is an octonion algebra.
proofSteps: For split O start from the split Albert algebra carrier TauCeti.AlbertAlgebra (its Jordan identity is a LieHighestWeight Layer 8 target) and the split E₇ Lie algebra of that layer; for a totally definite O over a totally real k construct J₃(O), its Koecher–Tits group and the commuting action of Aut(O) × PGSp₆ here.
Determine the commuting action on the off-diagonal entries, compare root lattices and localizations, and compute the k-rank from the definite octonion norm.
acceptance: The rank-three assertion belongs to the totally definite case; it is not asserted for the split global pair.

sources.match: Gan–Savin take a totally real field and a totally definite octonion algebra, form the adjoint group of type E₇ and k-rank 3 attached to J₃(O) by the Koecher–Tits construction, and use the dual pair G × PGSp₆ inside it (packet E19 for the definiteness hypothesis).
Savin's appendix constructs split adjoint E₇ from the split Albert algebra by the Koecher–Tits construction and describes its Siegel parabolic.

nodes.title: The global minimal residual representation
nodes.statement: For the rank-three Jordan E₇ family with r=3,d=8 in Hanzer–Savin normalization, the spherical degenerate Eisenstein family has simple poles at s=1,5,9; the residue at s=5 gives the nonzero square-integrable minimal automorphic representation, while s=9 gives the trivial constituent. Construct its adelic realization and identify its local components with the chosen minimal representations, including ramified and real forms.
hypotheses: k is a number field and the Jordan rank-three E₇ family is as in HS §6.2; use its normalized induction parameter.
proofSteps: Use the Jordan Gindikin–Karpelevich calculation for all constant terms and the cancellation analysis in Theorem 6.4 to prove nonzero simple residue at 5.
Apply the residual square-integrability criterion and identify the local spherical subquotients; verify the non-spherical local realization required by the kernel.
acceptance: The minimal residue is at 5 in this normalization; calling the last pole 9 minimal is incorrect.

sources.match: Hanzer–Savin show that for J_r(D) with d ≡ 0 mod 4 (automatic for r ≥ 3) the degenerate Eisenstein series has simple poles at 1, 1 + d/2, …, 1 + (r−1)d/2 with square-integrable residues equal to the co-socle of the degenerate principal series; for r = 3, d = 8 these are 1, 5, 9.

sources.locator: §4.1, Lemma 4.1, Corollary 4.2 and Proposition 4.3, pp. 190–191; remark after Corollary 4.6, p. 192; proof of Proposition 6.3, p. 197
sources.match: Hanzer–Savin compute the local c-function and reducibility points of the degenerate series, describe the spherical quotients, identify the quotient at 1 + (r−2)d/2 as a minimal representation in the quaternion case d = 4, and identify the trivial representation as the residue at the last pole. The identification of the minimal residue at 5 for d = 8 is part of gap G13.
Gan–Savin take the global minimal representation of the rank-three E₇ from Hanzer–Savin Theorem 6.4.

nodes.title: The global exceptional theta lift
nodes.statement: For a cusp form φ on G=Aut(O) and f in the global minimal automorphic representation, define Θ(f,φ)(h)=∫_[G] f(gh)overline(φ(g))dg. Prove absolute convergence, smoothness, automorphy, moderate growth and compatibility with the local theta quotient at every place. In the anisotropic case [G] is compact; for split G prove the estimates from cusp-form rapid decay and the minimal kernel’s growth. Define the global lift as the span of these functions, not as a presumed irreducible representation.
hypotheses: k is a number field; φ is a cuspidal automorphic form with the fixed unitary central conventions and f is a smooth automorphic minimal vector.
proofSteps: Use reduction theory to dominate the kernel by a fixed polynomial on Siegel sets, integrate against arbitrary rapid-decay order, and differentiate under a uniform integrable bound. Compare adelic translation with the local quotient universal property.
acceptance: A classical global oscillator integral does not define this exceptional kernel.

sources.match: Gross–Savin define the global lift from the anisotropic G₂ over ℚ to the rank-three E₇ partner by integrating an automorphic form against Kim's automorphic realization of the minimal representation, note convergence over the compact quotient, and compute its Fourier coefficients and cuspidality.
Savin's appendix defines the global lift for split G₂, notes absolute convergence from the cusp-form decay and moderate growth of the output, and unfolds its Whittaker coefficient.

nodes.title: A quaternion period forces global nonvanishing
nodes.statement: For totally real k and totally definite O, a cuspidal automorphic representation of G with nonzero GD period for some quaternion D⊂O has a nonzero exceptional global H lift. Prove the extension from the Q setting of Gross–Savin to this k setting by unfolding a full-rank Siegel coefficient of the kernel and choosing factorizable local test functions with nonzero orbit integrals.
hypotheses: k is totally real, O is totally definite, and an automorphic G representation has a nonzero GD period.
proofSteps: Identify the rational orbit of quaternion embeddings and its stabilizer, unfold over GD(k)∖G(k), and use compactness/convergence to interchange the integral and orbit sum. Replace the rational-number arithmetic choices by their number-field versions explicitly.
acceptance: A bare statement that the Q proof is unchanged does not establish the number-field extension.

sources.match: Gross–Savin show over ℚ that a nonzero period over the centralizer of a quaternion subalgebra is equivalent to the nonvanishing of the corresponding Fourier coefficient of the global lift.
Gan–Savin apply this over a totally real field to obtain nonzero global lifts; the node records the extension from ℚ as an obligation (gap G13).

nodes.title: Cuspidality from Steinberg or regular compact weight
nodes.statement: In the setting of the preceding period theorem, the nonzero global lift is cuspidal if its G input has a Steinberg component at one finite place or has regular highest weight at one real place. Prove both alternatives by calculating every proper H constant term; the real condition is regularity, not merely a nontrivial real representation.
hypotheses: k is totally real, O totally definite, and the GD period on the input representation is nonzero.
proofSteps: Compute the three maximal-parabolic constant terms using the global minimal representation and the associated lower lifts. In the finite-place case use Steinberg Jacquet exponents; in the real case use the compact highest-weight condition to kill all lower lift contributions.
acceptance: Verify all three maximal constant terms and the extension from Q to totally real k.

sources.match: Gan–Savin state that the global lift is cuspidal if the input has a Steinberg component at a finite place or regular highest weight at a real place.
Gross–Savin prove the corresponding cuspidality statement over ℚ.

nodes.title: Generic global nonvanishing
nodes.statement: For split G₂ over a number field k, every globally ψ-generic cuspidal input has a nonzero globally generic exceptional lift to PGSp₆. If one finite component is supercuspidal and its local H lift is supercuspidal, the global lift is cuspidal. This is a theta theorem for an existing automorphic input; it does not reproduce the separate globalization or G₂ LLC construction.
hypotheses: k is a number field; G₂ is split; the input is a globally generic cuspidal automorphic representation.
proofSteps: Unfold the generic H coefficient to the nonzero G₂ Whittaker coefficient using the rank-one Albert orbit.
Use the unramified spherical calculation outside a finite set and compactly supported local choices inside it to make the unfolded integral nonzero.
At the designated finite place local supercuspidality kills the proper H constant terms and gives cuspidality.
acceptance: The local supercuspidal-lift condition is required for the cuspidality clause.

sources.locator: Theorem A.9 and Lemma A.10, pp. 28–30
sources.match: Savin's appendix shows that a cusp form on split G₂ with nonzero Whittaker coefficient has a global lift with nonzero Whittaker coefficient, using the unramified local computation of Lemma A.10.
Gan–Savin use this together with a supercuspidal local lift to obtain globally generic cuspidal lifts.

nodes.title: Real infinitesimal-character matching
nodes.statement: For the real exceptional G₂×PGSp₆ dual pair in E₇, construct the map on Harish–Chandra central characters induced by the minimal representation and prove that every occurring real theta pair has matched infinitesimal characters. Give its weight-coordinate formula with the chosen positive roots and ρ shifts. Combined with the imported unitary-dual theorem sufficiently far from the walls, this implies discrete-series real H components for the global input used in LL §8.4.
hypotheses: The field is R and the local minimal representation is the real E₇ model for the stated dual pair.
proofSteps: Compute the two centers in the annihilator quotient of the real minimal Harish–Chandra module; compare the Cartan polynomials and the ρ-shifted parameters. Import the appropriate real unitary-dual isolation theorem only after checking its good-range bound.
acceptance: The exact central-character map and distance-from-walls bound remain source-verification gaps; no unverified coordinate formula is inserted.

sources.match: Gan–Savin invoke the matching of infinitesimal characters for the real dual pair (citing Huang–Pandžić–Savin) and the fact that unitary representations with discrete-series infinitesimal character sufficiently far from the walls are discrete series.

upstreamAudit.result: Current TauCetiRoadmap main and the current TauCeti library were inspected read-only in addition to the atlas audit. Existing octonion arithmetic, generic exceptional Lie/Albert constructions, spin/triality, compact branching and the local Weil group are imported. None of the nine named roadmaps postdating the atlas snapshot supplies the exceptional minimal representations or this Howe proof.

upstreamNotes.note: Pull request #785 states Whittaker multiplicity one only for GL₂ (SR.2.3) and has no Plancherel or Schwartz-algebra theory. Several atlas roadmaps, this one included, use multiplicity one of Whittaker models for quasi-split groups (G₂, PGSp₆) and the Harish-Chandra–Silberger reducibility criterion; they are requested from an undesigned Part II.

Pull request #1063 has §3.38a (the restricted Mp₂ × G₂ oscillator, Gan–Gurevich) which the atlas packet MetaplecticAutomorphicForms--MP.0 does not yet carry as a node; this roadmap cites it through the stage MetaplecticAutomorphicForms:MP.3.

review.notes: Independent review of the Codex design (DESIGN-ExceptionalThetaCorrespondencesForG2, PR #10607). Every locator was located by a retrieval sweep; the reviewer read GS §§2–9, 11, 13 and 15, the cited passages of the other sources and every flagged row; statements are faithful, with the paper extractions’ confirmed corrections applied. Every match had been a verbatim copy of the node statement; all 96 were rewritten in the reviewer’s own words, and locators that mixed two sources under one sourceId (Sav, GS04, MS, Pra, GrS, LL inside GS or HKT entries) were split. Locator errors fixed: GrS Proposition 4.5 p. 200, GS §6.4 pp. 20–21, Lemma 11.3 (no Lemma 11.2), the Steinberg assignment in Theorem 8.5. The roadmap no longer lists itself as a prerequisite; stage requires were recomputed from node prerequisites. sourceIssues E1–E20 confirmed at their locators. The reader was regenerated from the corrected packet (its 24 stray emphasis spans removed).
